findings.source_quote: ἐπεὶ οὖν οἱ πιστεύσαντες ἐκ τοῦ ὄρους τούτου πάντες ἄκακοι εὑρέθησαν, ἐκέλευσεν ὁ κύριος τοῦ πύργου τούτους ἐκ τῶν ῥιζῶν τοῦ ὄρους τούτου βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τοῦ πύργου
findings.english_quote: Since all the believers from this mountain were found innocent, the Lord of the tower ordered that these stones from the mountain’s roots be put into the tower’s building.
findings.issue: The translation follows the selected working text, but its notes do not distinguish the editorially supplied τῶν ῥιζῶν in paragraph 2 from preserved wording. The supplied apparatus transcription attributes that insertion to Hilgenfeld and reports its omission in A. It also identifies the first τούτου as Harmer’s conjecture against τοῦ λευκοῦ in A. These local editorial choices remain undisclosed despite the detailed disclosure of the correction in paragraph 3.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the selected working reading, but add an attributed apparatus note explaining that paragraph 2’s 'roots' wording includes an editorial insertion reported absent in Athos, and that its first 'this mountain' follows a printed conjecture where Athos is reported to read 'the white mountain.' Distinguish these reports from fresh manuscript verification.

findings.english_quote: The apparatus proposes wording about recognizing their servitude from versions and Latin variants, but this draft does not silently adopt that conjecture.
findings.issue: This definite description of the apparatus proposal is not reconciled with the supplied evidence. The earlier comparison report gives posse servitatem (or servitutem) agnoscere, but the separately supplied attributed apparatus transcription gives posse securitatem (or severitatem) agentes. Those are materially different proposals. Footnote c and the lexical alternative 'recognize their servitude' present only the earlier account without disclosing the conflict.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the provisional translation of the dagger-marked working text. Revise footnote c and the lexical metadata to disclose that the supplied reports disagree about the apparatus proposal and that its wording remains unverified. Do not identify 'recognize their servitude' as the established apparatus alternative unless additional evidence reconciles the conflicting transcriptions. Any replacement note or alternative requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἐπεὶ οὖν οἱ πιστεύσαντες ἐκ τοῦ ὄρους τούτου πάντες ἄκακοι εὑρέθησαν, ἐκέλευσεν ὁ κύριος τοῦ πύργου τούτους ἐκ τῶν ῥιζῶν τοῦ ὄρους τούτου βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τοῦ πύργου
findings.english_quote: All the believers from this mountain were found innocent. So the Lord of the tower ordered stones from its roots to be put into the building.
findings.issue: The simplified wording follows the selected working text, but its notes leave paragraph 2’s editorial supplementation undisclosed. The supplied apparatus transcription identifies τῶν ῥιζῶν as Hilgenfeld’s insertion, reported absent in A, and the first τούτου as Harmer’s conjecture against τοῦ λευκοῦ in A. The existing notes do not distinguish these choices from preserved wording.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the working reading and add a reader-accessible note identifying the reported editorial insertion behind paragraph 2’s 'roots' wording and the reported 'white mountain' alternative behind its first 'this mountain.' Attribute the information to the supplied apparatus transcription rather than claiming manuscript verification.

findings.english_quote: The apparatus proposes wording about recognizing their servitude from versions and Latin variants, but this draft does not silently adopt that conjecture.
findings.issue: The simplified edition independently retains the same unresolved evidentiary conflict: the earlier report describes a servitude-recognition conjecture, while the supplied attributed apparatus transcription instead records posse securitatem (or severitatem) agentes. Footnote c and the lexical alternative 'recognize their servitude' do not disclose that disagreement and therefore overstate the established content of the apparatus.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the provisional main-text rendering and its uncertainty marker. State that the supplied reports disagree about the proposed correction, and qualify or remove the definite servitude-recognition alternative pending evidence that reconciles them. Review any replacement wording afresh.

summary: Both editions cover the selected Greek and Latin clauses and preserve the principal conditions, necessity, negations, speaker attribution, and difficult assertions. Neither requires replacement of the disclosed working reading merely because alternatives exist. Both require revision of their editorial disclosures: paragraph 2’s supplementation is unmarked, and the account of the paragraph 5 apparatus proposal overlooks conflicting supplied transcriptions. This review assesses the supplied text and attributed reports, not unseen manuscripts or an exhaustive collation.
